name: reflection-architecture
context: The Reflection pattern enables runtime adaptation by maintaining a causally-connected self-representation. It separates a base-level (application logic) from a meta-level (reflective entities) with a causal connection between them, allowing the system to inspect and modify its own structure and behavior at runtime.
benefits: Zero-downtime adaptation: Change behavior without restart
Self-healing: System can detect and fix issues at runtime
Dynamic configuration: Modify behavior based on runtime conditions
Extensibility: Add new capabilities without redeployment
Runtime introspection: Inspect system state and structure dynamically
Policy separation: Business rules separated from implementation
tradeoffs: Performance overhead: Reflection adds runtime overhead for introspection and modification
Complexity: Meta-level architecture significantly increases system complexity
Security risks: Exposed internals increase attack surface if not properly secured
Debugging difficulty: Harder to trace and debug reflective operations
Learning curve: Requires deep understanding of reflective concepts
Tooling limitations: Some IDEs and tools have limited support for reflective code
use_cases: Systems that cannot tolerate downtime and require zero-downtime updates
Runtime adaptation required based on environmental conditions
Highly configurable business logic that changes frequently
Long-running platforms (space rovers, autonomous robots, NASA missions)
Self-monitoring and self-healing traffic monitoring cameras
avoid_when: Simple CRUD applications with stable requirements
Performance-critical hot paths where every cycle counts
Security-sensitive code without careful security boundaries
Teams lacking experience with reflective programming
Systems requiring strong static typing guarantees
component_types: Meta-Object Protocol (MOP) Interface: Standard interface for all reflective operations
Architectural Meta-Entities: Maintain runtime representation of software architecture
Behavioral Meta-Entities: Reflect on method calls, execution flow, state machines
Self-Representation Repository: Stores the causally-connected self-model
Reflection Controller: Manages level shifts and meta-level computations
Monitoring Agent: Observes base-level and triggers reflective actions
anti_patterns: Excessive reflection: Using MOP for operations better handled statically
Tight coupling: Meta and base levels too interdependent
Uncontrolled introspection: Exposing sensitive internals without access controls
Reflection without encapsulation: Breaking the mirror design principles
Distributed monolith via reflection: Using reflection to create inappropriate dependencies
Single-layer reflection: Only reflecting on one level when multiple levels needed
design_principles: Encapsulation: Meta-level facilities must encapsulate their implementation details from base-level components
Stratification: Meta-level must be cleanly separated from base-level functionality: no leakage of concerns
Ontological Correspondence: Meta-level ontology should correspond to the language it manipulates: the reflection model should mirror actual system structure
Causal Connection: Changes to meta-level data structures must immediately reflect on the actual system and vice versa
Minimal Entry Points: Limit reflective access to well-defined interfaces to reduce attack surface
Cache Metadata: Cache reflectively obtained metadata to reduce repeated introspection overhead
best_practices: Limit Reflection Usage: Use reflection only when alternatives (interfaces, Strategy pattern) are not possible
Cache Metadata Lookups: Avoid repeated reflective calls; cache metadata through static fields or caches
Use Interfaces: Code against interfaces to avoid breakage due to implementation changes
Enable Selectively: Only enable access via `setAccessible()` for specific members, not blanket permissions
Validate Permissions: Check runtime permissions before allowing reflective access
Protect Entry Points: Guard public APIs enabling reflection to prevent misuse
Keep Reflection Narrow: Use reflection only where runtime uncertainty is unavoidable, keep core domain logic typed
Descriptor Caching: Parse once at startup, build cached descriptors, run fast code paths from descriptors
Handle Errors Properly: Always handle exceptions such as `NoSuchMethodException`, `IllegalAccessException`, `InvocationTargetException`
